metadata.note: Two separate railroads, three separate lines, all converging on Green Bay: the Chicago & North Western operated two distinct physical routes north from Milwaukee -- the inland Valley Line via the Fox River Valley (Fond du Lac-Oshkosh-Appleton) and the coastal Lake Shore Line, which hugs Lake Michigan through Sheboygan and Manitowoc before turning inland via Francis Creek-Maribel-Denmark-Bellevue to Green Bay -- while the separate Milwaukee Road took a third route east of Lake Winnebago via Plymouth and Chilton. All three carried Green Bay's passenger traffic until Amtrak's 1971 creation, after which none were retained -- Green Bay has had no intercity passenger rail since. The Valley Line's geometry is traced through real track using OpenStreetMap data (Overpass API) and shortest-path graph search, since that corridor remains active rail today. The Lake Shore Line and Milwaukee Road geometries are hand-placed waypoints through the real historic station towns each line served (confirmed via a period C&NW station list for the Lake Shore Line -- Sheboygan, Manitowoc, Francis Creek, Maribel, Denmark, Bellevue -- rather than a naive straight line, which had incorrectly cut across the Bay of Green Bay via Kewaunee, a separate branch railroad, not this mainline), not surveyed track centerline -- the Overpass API was unreachable/overloaded for repeated attempts at these two corridors (confirmed still-severed even after the API recovered: Sheboygan's nearest trackage today is an isolated 2-node fragment, disconnected from the wider network), and unlike the Valley Line, large stretches of both may no longer be intact active rail to trace even with full API access.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.rule4_split: 2026-08-30: the single 'Milwaukee and Northern Railway / Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific Railroad' feature was one feature in one colour (#F58220) across an ownership change, and that colour matched no other Milwaukee Road feature in the repo (five features elsewhere at #C25E00). Split at 1893 into two features sharing identical geometry, per Rule 4. SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded rather than resolved: this layer's original note dated the absorption into the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul to 1884, while research/branches/chicago_milwaukee_st_paul_and_pacific_railroad.txt (block [19] and its ownership_split section) dates it to 1893. The split here is drawn at 1893, the research report's date; if 1884 is right, nine years of this line are drawn in the wrong company's colour and the fix is to move the split, not to recolour.

properties.line: Milwaukee and Northern: Milwaukee – Green Bay
properties.geometry_quality: STRAIGHT LINE, not a trace: the whole feature is five hand-placed waypoints through Milwaukee, the Cedarburg/Plymouth corridor and Green Bay -- roughly 120 mi of ruled line, 100% of the feature -- carried over unchanged from before this split. OSM does carry the Milwaukee Road's Milwaukee - Green Bay grade, so this is a cheap fix for a later pass; it was not done here because this edit is a Rule 4 ownership split, not a retrace. The line as drawn also stops at Green Bay: the real service continued to Iron Mountain, Channing and (as the Copper Country Limited) Calumet, which is not drawn anywhere.

The split here is drawn at 1893, the research report's date; if 1884 is right, nine years of this line are drawn in the wrong company's colour and the fix is to move the split, not to recolour.

segments.note: Milwaukee Road operation: the Milwaukee & Northern was absorbed into the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul in 1893, which is why these years carry the Milwaukee Road's colour rather than the Milwaukee & Northern's. Absorbed into the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul Railway (later the Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific, 'the Milwaukee Road') in 1884; continued beyond Green Bay to Channing in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, with two daily round trips per a 1952 timetable; the original 1898 Green Bay depot was donated to the city in 1957, though sources differ on whether train service itself continued from another facility until Amtrak's broader 1971 cutover; frequency estimated, unsourced END-YEAR CAUTION: the research report can only prove passenger service to 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide Table 20, printed times) and records the end as unknown-after-1951, commonly cited as the Copper Country Limited's 1968 withdrawal. The 1971 end drawn here is this layer's original figure and is NOT verified; it is the one date in this feature most likely to be overstating service.
